critical_code_review_comments: ReportIn.description has NO min_length validation in pydantic (server.py ~399). Spec requires min 20 chars but backend will accept any non-empty string. Currently enforced only client-side in ReportModal — backend should add `Field(min_length=20, max_length=2000)` to prevent API-direct abuse.

POST /api/reports admits role 'admin' would 403 with 'Only clients and providers can report' — good — but `target_role` in payload is NOT cross-checked against `target.role` from DB. A malicious actor can send target_role='client' while target is actually a provider; this corrupts admin filters (?target_role=client returns mixed entities). Suggestion: server should overwrite `target_role` from `target['role']`.

Auto-flag at ≥3/90d (server.py ~1119) only flips users.flagged_by_reports=true; it never resets to false after admin dismisses reports. Over time every user may end up flagged forever. Consider recomputing on admin actions or on a daily job.
/api/admin/reports `flagged_users` count includes users with is_deleted=true. Likely should exclude deleted/suspended users to reflect actionable queue.

SEO content endpoint generates lazily per (cat,city). With 184 cats × 23 cities = 4232 possible pages, the first crawl by Google will trigger 4232 LLM calls. Consider a background pre-warm job or rate-limit/queue.
server.py is now ~3733 lines — still growing. Sprint 1 review already flagged this; Sprint 2 added another ~120 lines without modularization.
